newsitem.title: UK: UK's Fergie tries career as radio show host - BBC.
newsitem.headline: UK's Fergie tries career as radio show host - BBC.

text.p: Britain's Duchess of York may have found herself a new career as a radio chat show host, the BBC said on Friday.
The Duchess, best known as Fergie, has been talking to the international arm of BBC radio about the possibility of having her own programme.
"The programme has not been commissioned, it's at a very early stage," a BBC spokesman told Reuters.
He said that if any programmes were made, they would be transmitted overseas.

Saturday's Independent newspaper said Fergie had been working on a pilot programme for nearly four months at the BBC's London headquarters and had already interviewed a number of celebrities, including Italian opera star Luciano Pavarotti and soap actress Joan Collins.
It said Fergie herself had asked that the programmes should not be broadcast in Britain, at least initially.
The BBC was negotiating to sell the chat shows to American radio, the Independent said. It quoted a BBC spokeswoman as saying: "We needed to raise our profile in the U.S. radio market."
Fergie has embarked on a variety of ventures since her divorce last year from Queen Elizabeth's second son, Prince Andrew.
She has published an autobiography, conducted book signings around the world and taken modelling assignments, partly to pay off her huge debts.
